checks.do: Whether the SCIM-enabled IdP is selected and the time filter covers the change, which is limited to the last two weeks.
Which entity, method and status code the entry shows, filtering on the entity or its internal ID.

what.statement: SCIM Sync Logs are the audit of operations between the IdP and the SCIM service; operations that change the state of users and groups appear on the SCIM Sync Logs page. They are used to troubleshoot group membership or user attribute updates, and a SCIM-enabled IdP is selected to list the logs.

quotes: SCIM Sync Logs are the audit of operations between the identity provider (IdP) and the SCIM service. Operations that change the state of the users and groups are presented on the SCIM Sync Logs page.
Troubleshoot issues with group membership or user attribute updates.
Select a SCIM-enabled IdP to generate a list of SCIM logs in the table.

time-range.statement: The table can be filtered over a period between 7 Days and 14 Days or a Custom Range whose start and end date must be within the last two weeks; by default it is set to two weeks.

quotes: Filter the information that appears in the table over a period between 7 Days and 14 Days, or you can select Custom Range. If you use a Custom Range, the start and end date must be within the last two weeks. By default, this is set to two weeks.

filters.statement: The filters are Entity Name, IdP SCIM Entity ID, Internal Entity ID, Payload Search Entity ID, Entity Type (user or group), Response Status Code (200, 201, 204, 400, 403, 404, 409), HTTP Method (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), and response duration of up to 200 milliseconds, up to 500 milliseconds, up to 1 second, up to 3 seconds or more than 3 seconds. By default no filters are selected.

quotes: By default, no filters are selected.
IdP SCIM Entity ID: The IdP SCIM entity ID for the user or group obtained from the IdP.
Internal Entity ID: The internal ID for the user or group is obtained from the IdP, which is generated by the Private Access SCIM service.
Payload Search Entity ID: The internal ID that matches either the entity ID resource or is part of an associated user or group resource.
Entity Type: The type of the entity (i.e., user or group).
Response Status Code: The HTTP status code in the response (i.e., 200, 201, 204, 400, 403, 404, 409).
HTTP Method: The type of the HTTP method (i.e., POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE).
Up to 200 milliseconds
Up to 500 milliseconds
Up to 1 second
Up to 3 seconds
More than 3 seconds

evidence.after: By default, no filters are selected.
quotes: Entity Name: The name of the entity (i.e., User Name, Group Name).

columns.statement: Each log entry shows Request Time, Request (the HTTP method and URL endpoint), Entity (type and internal ID), IdP SCIM Entity ID, Response Duration (ms) and Status Code.

quotes: Request Time: The date and time of the request.
Request (Method - URL): The type of HTTP method (i.e., POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) and the URL endpoint.
Entity (Type: Internal Entity ID): The internal ID for the user or group.
IdP SCIM Entity ID:The IdP SCIM Entity ID for the user or group obtained from the IdP.
Response Duration (ms): The duration of the response in milliseconds.
Status Code: The HTTP status code associated with the request.

details.statement: The View icon opens the Sync Log Details drawer, which shows the GID and request details.

quotes: Click the View icon () to open the Sync Log Details drawer and see the GID and request details.

retention.title: How long SCIM sync log entries are kept
retention.detail: The filter window is at most two weeks; the page does not say how long entries are retained beyond it.

status-code-meanings.title: What each filterable status code means for a push
status-code-meanings.detail: The page lists 200, 201, 204, 400, 403, 404 and 409 as status codes to filter on, and the Internal Entity ID description contradicts itself (obtained from the IdP, but generated by the Private Access SCIM service); neither says what any code means for a push.
